underdog-victory.name: Underdog Victory
underdog-victory.summary: Story arc of someone or something overlooked who triumphs in the end. Useful for founder narratives, brand stories, and team-building decks where the lesson is about resilience and unexpected wins.

beats.name: Origin
beats.description: Establish the opening scene: who the underdog is and the world that overlooked them. Specific details make the rest of the journey feel real.

beats.name: Struggles
beats.description: Highlight the early setbacks. What didn't work, who said no, where the path closed up. The audience needs to feel the doubt before they can feel the win.

beats.name: Determination
beats.description: Showcase the enduring passion that kept the underdog going. What they refused to give up on, and why. Determination, in this beat, is the only resource the underdog has.

beats.name: Crisis
beats.description: Identify the lowest point of the journey. The moment the dream nearly ended. Don't soften — the contrast with the triumph ahead depends on the depth of this slide.

beats.name: Resolve
beats.description: Articulate the choice the underdog made to keep going. The strong will, the small bet, the borrowed faith. Resolve is where the protagonist becomes someone the audience roots for.

beats.name: Breakthrough
beats.description: Show the reward of perseverance: the customer who said yes, the door that opened, the fortune that turned. The breakthrough should feel earned, not granted.

beats.name: Triumph
beats.description: Reveal the ultimate success. Concrete outcomes, named milestones. The triumph is the audience's emotional payoff — let it land.

beats.name: Legacy
beats.description: Share the lasting impact. What the underdog's victory makes possible for those who come after. The legacy beat is what turns a story into a lesson.

media.name: Media & Press
media.summary: Journalists, analysts, and media professionals seeking newsworthy insights and quotable statistics.
media.description: Journalists, analysts, and media professionals looking for newsworthy insight and quotable statistics. Make headline numbers prominent, attribute every figure clearly, design for print, and add embargo notes when needed. Moderate chart density; 8-12 slides in press-kit format.

decide.name: Drive a Decision
decide.summary: Frame options, evidence, tradeoffs, and a recommendation so the audience can choose.
decide.description: Use when the deck exists to get a yes/no, select among options, approve a recommendation, or resolve ambiguity. Lead with the decision needed and make the ask explicit.
decide.outcome: The audience makes or authorizes a clear decision.

authoritative.name: Authoritative
authoritative.summary: Expert, declarative voice for category-defining and analyst-style decks.
authoritative.description: Adopt the perspective of someone who's seen the full landscape and is willing to call it. Use plain declaratives — strong claims with the receipts to back them. Step back from internal-only context and frame in terms the wider industry would recognize.
voiceCues: Use declarative sentences; trust the reader to follow.
Frame in industry-wide terms, not company-internal language.
Cite outside sources — analysts, benchmarks, public peers.
Take a position; avoid 'on the other hand' symmetry without a verdict.
avoid: Hedging ('we believe', 'in our view') unless deliberately contrasting.
First-person plural overload — speak for the work, not the team.
Tentative phrasing that softens strong claims.
samplePhrases: Agent latency is the bottleneck of the next AI cycle.
Three categories will absorb 80% of enterprise budget; we're built for the second.
The benchmarks are public; the gap holds across every comparable workload.

minimal.name: Minimal
minimal.description: A clean, minimalistic theme with a focus on simplicity and readability. Ideal for professional, straightforward presentations.

forest-green.name: Forest Green
forest-green.summary: Organic green palette for growth, health, and sustainability stories.
forest-green.description: A green and soft-neutral scheme for decks about growth, renewal, wellness, and environmental impact.

cool-horizon.name: Cool Horizon
cool-horizon.summary: Cool blue-green palette tuned for professional business decks.
cool-horizon.description: A balanced cool-toned scheme with deep navy, business blues, and teal accents. It works well across strategy, finance, and technical narratives.

aptos.name: Aptos
aptos.description: Aptos is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Aptos Display for headings with Aptos for body text.

cover.name: Cover
cover.summary: The opening slide: title, subtitle and an optional picture.
cover.description: Open a presentation with its subject and a short introduction. Add a picture when it helps establish the context.

text.name: Text
text.summary: Prose. Several blocks sit side by side when short and stack when long.
text.description: Explain one idea in continuous prose. Use paragraphs or flowing blocks for detail that needs to be read in sequence.

chart.name: Chart
chart.summary: One to six charts, with an optional note.
chart.description: Give a chart enough space to show its evidence. Use the title to state the conclusion and labels to explain the measures.

list.name: List
list.summary: Bulleted or numbered points; one long list flows into columns.
list.description: Present several related points in a clear sequence. Use bullets for independent points or numbered items for an ordered list.
